pharm: Long-acting oxytocin analogue that selectively binds uterine oxytocin receptors to produce rhythmic then sustained tonic uterine contraction, reducing postpartum blood loss.

summary: Carbetocin is a long-acting synthetic analogue of oxytocin used to prevent uterine atony and postpartum hemorrhage after delivery, classically following caesarean section under spinal or epidural anaesthesia and after vaginal delivery in appropriate settings. A single 100 microgram dose produces a prolonged uterotonic effect compared with oxytocin, with onset of firm contraction within about 2 minutes. It must be given only AFTER delivery of the infant and must never be used to induce or augment labour. It is contraindicated during pregnancy/before delivery, in serious cardiovascular disease, epilepsy, and significant hepatic or renal disease. Common effects are nausea, abdominal pain, flushing, hypotension, headache, and tremor. (Note: carbetocin is approved in the EU/UK and many other regions but is not FDA-approved in the United States; data are drawn from the EMA/SmPC.)

moa: Carbetocin is a long-acting synthetic octapeptide analogue of oxytocin. It selectively binds to oxytocin receptors on uterine smooth muscle, triggering rhythmic uterine contractions, increasing the frequency of existing contractions, and raising uterine tone. Compared with oxytocin, structural modifications give it a longer duration of action, so a single dose produces sustained uterine contraction with onset of firm tone within about 2 minutes, helping to compress uterine vessels and reduce postpartum blood loss. It acts predominantly on the puerperal (post-delivery) uterus, which has increased oxytocin-receptor density.

Use to induce or augment labour

preg: Carbetocin is contraindicated during pregnancy and must not be used before delivery of the infant or to induce or augment labour; it is intended solely for use immediately after delivery to prevent uterine atony.
lact: Only small amounts of carbetocin pass into breast milk and these are likely degraded in the infant gut; breastfeeding may be continued after a single postpartum dose.
renal: Carbetocin is contraindicated in significant renal disease.
hepatic: Carbetocin is contraindicated in significant hepatic disease.

moderate: Other oxytocics / ergot alkaloids (e.g., ergometrine) and prostaglandins - additive uterotonic effect; combined use should be deliberate and monitored
Drugs prolonging the QT interval or potent vasoconstrictors used in obstetric anaesthesia - monitor cardiovascular status
minor: Inhalation anaesthetics may reduce the uterotonic effect
interactions.alcohol: Not applicable in the acute obstetric setting.
interactions.diagnostics: Excessive intravenous fluids with oxytocics can cause dilutional hyponatraemia; monitor fluid balance.

serious: Excessive uterine bleeding if atony not controlled
rare: Water intoxication/hyponatraemia (mainly with excess IV fluids)

monitoring: Uterine tone and amount of vaginal bleeding
Blood pressure and heart rate during and after administration
Fluid balance to avoid dilutional hyponatraemia
Need for additional uterotonics if bleeding persists
counsel: This medicine is given by your obstetric team as a single injection right after your baby is born
It helps your womb contract to reduce bleeding after delivery
You may feel warm, flushed, nauseated, or have a brief headache or tremor shortly after the injection
Tell your team if you feel faint, very short of breath, or develop a rash or swelling
You can continue to breastfeed after receiving this medicine
pk: Firm uterine contraction within about 2 minutes of IV injection
Peak plasma concentration ~30 minutes after intramuscular dosing
Sustained uterine effect for roughly 1 hour, longer than oxytocin
Store below 30 C and do not freeze (some formulations refrigerated 2-8 C); use immediately after opening
pearls: Single 100 microgram dose gives a longer uterotonic effect than repeated oxytocin - no infusion needed
Give ONLY after delivery of the infant; never to induce or augment labour
Contraindicated in serious cardiovascular disease, eclampsia/pre-eclampsia, epilepsy, and significant hepatic/renal disease
Onset of firm contraction within ~2 minutes; watch for transient hypotension and flushing
Heat-stable formulations are used in WHO-recommended PPH prevention programs in low-resource settings
Not FDA-approved in the United States - data are from the EMA/SmPC (e.g., Pabal/Duratocin); oxytocin is the US standard
missed: Not applicable - carbetocin is given as a single dose by the obstetric team immediately after delivery and is not self-administered or repeated.
overdose: Overdose or excessive uterine stimulation can cause hyperstimulation with strong, prolonged uterine contractions, and with large intravenous fluid volumes may cause water intoxication and hyponatraemia. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive, including stopping any concomitant oxytocics, restricting fluids, correcting electrolytes, supporting blood pressure and respiration, and treating uterine hyperstimulation symptomatically.
